mappings.note: Translating 'adding 10 to a number gives 20' into an equation is the formulation half of LO-6 (solve puzzles and daily life problems using variables); the chapter's pure symbol-manipulation items are kept at competency level instead, so the two kinds are distinguishable.
Statement-to-equation translation, so LO-6 rather than C-MAT2.1: a variable has to be introduced to model the statement.
Statement-to-equation translation with subtraction; LO-6 for the modelling step.
'Seven times a number is 42' modelled as 7x = 42 -> LO-6.
'Divided by 5 gives 6' modelled as x/5 = 6 -> LO-6.
'Subtracted from 40 results in 15' modelled as 40 - x = 15; LO-6, and the order of subtraction is the point being tested.
Two-step statement (3x + 6 = 15) modelled as an equation -> LO-6.
Two-step statement (2x - 30 = 56) modelled as an equation -> LO-6.

Find the root of z + 4 = -8: no context and nothing to model, so this is technique rather than LO-6's puzzle/daily-life work. The frame has no LO for solving a given linear equation, so the competency is the nearest legal citation.
Solve 3x = 20/7 - x; variables on both sides, still pure technique -> competency, not LO-6.
2x + 3 = 2(x - 4) has no solution; the item tests recognising that, which is technique -> competency.
5/x = 2 is not linear as written but is solved by the same transposition; technique -> competency.
Expressing the smallest of three consecutive numbers when the largest is x + 1 is a number puzzle handled with a variable -> LO-6, not LO-7 (there is no product to expand).
Representing the next even number after x is variable-based puzzle representation -> LO-6.
Representing the preceding odd number before x -> LO-6; tests x - 2 rather than x - 1.
Smaller number as x - 21 given a difference of 21 -> LO-6 representation.
Place-value representation 10y + x of a two-digit number is the classic variable puzzle -> LO-6.
Stem is fraction-flattened ('-2/3 = 2x is 3'), but it is plainly asking for x in a one-step equation; technique -> competency. Flagged as garbled.
3y + 4 = 5y - 4, variables both sides; technique -> competency.
(2x - 1) + (x - 1) = x + 2 requires collecting like terms then transposing; technique -> competency, not LO-7 since nothing is multiplied out.
11x - 5 - x + 6 = 2x + 17, collect and transpose; technique -> competency.
Complementary angles differing by 10 degrees is modelled as x + (x + 10) = 90 -> LO-6. Not LO-11, which is specifically the angle sum of a quadrilateral.
Supplementary angles in ratio 1:2 modelled as x + 2x = 180 -> LO-6; again not LO-11, no quadrilateral involved.
Sum 23, difference 3: two-unknown word problem reduced to one variable -> LO-6.
Five consecutive naturals summing to 65 -> LO-6 consecutive-number puzzle.
Age problem twelve years hence versus twelve years ago -> LO-6 daily-life problem using a variable.
Printed as '3/x+8=4/6-x'; the text layer has dropped the brackets of 3/(x+8) = 4/(6-x). Mapped on the cross-multiplying technique it is reaching for -> competency. Flagged as garbled.
Ratio 3:8 with sum 165 is solved by letting the parts be 3x and 8x -> LO-6. Not LO-10: nothing varies in proportion here, it is a single partition.
Sum 69, difference 17 word problem -> LO-6.
Equation with fractional coefficients (the text layer has lost the bracketing of the numerators); technique of clearing denominators -> competency.
Classifying which candidate is NOT linear in one variable; the options are not stored, and no LO covers classifying equations, so the competency is cited.
Recall of the standard form ax + b = 0; definitional, no LO covers it -> competency.
Identify the linear equation in one variable; options absent, classification not covered by any LO -> competency.
Degree of x^2 - 2x + 1 = x^2 - 3 after the squared terms cancel; a recognition item about equation form, not LO-7's expansion of products -> competency.
